html:
A long Latin poem by Ovid, finished around 8 CE, that strings together more than 250 Greek and Roman myths about bodies changing shape. Its fifteen books run from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar.

Many famous stories come to us mainly through it: Daphne turning into a laurel tree to escape Apollo, Narcissus falling in love with his reflection, Pygmalion's statue coming to life, Icarus flying too close to the sun, Pyramus and Thisbe. Ovid tells them with wit, speed and sympathy for the victims of the gods.

In 8 CE Augustus banished Ovid to Tomis, on the Black Sea coast in today's Romania, for what Ovid called "a poem and a mistake". The poem was probably his cheeky Art of Love; the mistake is unknown. He died in exile.

The Metamorphoses became a storehouse of myth for later artists and writers. Shakespeare drew on it for A Midsummer Night's Dream and much else, and painters and sculptors from Titian to Bernini took their subjects from it.
sum: A long Latin poem by Ovid, finished around 8 CE, that strings together more than 250 Greek and Roman myths about bodies changing shape. Its fifteen books run from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar.
